The '''[[1949 in association football|1949]]–[[1950 in association football|50]] season''' was the 51st completed season of [[The Football League]].

==Final league tables==

The tables below are reproduced here in the exact form that they can be found at [https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1949-50.html The Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation] website<ref name="rsssf">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/engpaul/FLA/1949-50.html |title=England 1949-50 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref> and in ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79'',<ref name=" Rothmans"/> with home and away statistics separated.

Beginning with the season 1894–95, clubs finishing level on points were separated according to goal average (goals scored divided by goals conceded), or more properly put, goal ratio. In case one or more teams had the same goal difference, this system favoured those teams who had scored fewer goals. The goal average system was eventually scrapped beginning with the 1976–77 season.

From the 1922–23 season, the bottom two teams of both Third Division North and Third Division South were required to apply for [[re-election (Football League)|re-election]].<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>

[[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] retained the First Division title, finishing level on points with [[Wolverhampton Wanderers]]. [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] finished a single point behind the leading pair, with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] completing the top five. Sixth placed [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], the 1948 champions, finished four points off the top of the table but beat [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] to win their first postwar [[FA Cup]].

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] went down to the Second Division.
